intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Boat Tour
experiences.description: Hop between the stunning Phi Phi islands including Maya Bay, Monkey Beach, and Viking Cave. Snorkel in crystal-clear turquoise waters, explore dramatic limestone karsts, and swim in hidden lagoons. Full-day speedboat tours cover multiple islands with snorkeling gear included.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Walk
experiences.description: Explore Bangkok's legendary street food scene through Yaowarat Chinatown and the surrounding alleys. Sample pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, boat noodles, and fresh seafood from open-air stalls. Join a guided food tour or wander independently through the bustling night markets.

experiences.name: Railay Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Accessible only by longtail boat, Railay Beach is one of Thailand's most breathtaking coastal gems. Surrounded by towering limestone cliffs, enjoy pristine white sand beaches, kayaking through sea caves, and rock climbing. Explore both Railay West and East beaches and hike to the hidden lagoon viewpoint.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Island Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a day or two on the laid-back island of Koh Lanta, known for its long sandy beaches, vibrant coral reefs, and relaxed atmosphere. Rent a scooter to explore the island's coastline, visit the Old Town pier village with its Sino-Portuguese architecture, and snorkel at the Koh Lanta Marine National Park.

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Sunday Night Market & Street Food
experiences.description: Stroll through the famous Walking Street along Wualai Road every Sunday evening. Browse handmade crafts, local artwork, and textiles while feasting on northern Thai street food specialties like khao soi curry noodles, sai oua sausage, and crispy pork rinds. A perfect blend of culture, shopping, and authentic local flavors.
experiences.location: Wualai Road, Old City, Chiang Mai

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at destination airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, then take a budget shared minivan or bus transfer toward Krabi or Ao Nang pier. Board a longtail boat or ferry to Phi Phi Islands (approx. 1.5–2 hours). Check in to your boutique stay on Phi Phi Don and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along Tonsai Village to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Tonsai Village night scene. Browse the colorful street food stalls along the main walking street. Watch the sunset from the beach near the pier area.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during the flight — grab a snack or light meal onboard.
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick affordable bite at the airport or ferry terminal — look for a rice box or noodle soup for under 60 THB.
meals.dinner: Street food stalls in Tonsai Village — try pad thai, grilled satay skewers, and fresh spring rolls. Budget around 150–200 THB total.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and settling in. Don't overplan — rest is important after a long flight. Exchange some cash at the airport for better rates or use an ATM. Keep 500–1000 THB in hand for transfers and tips.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (Koh Phi Phi Don Viewpoint). The climb takes about 20–30 minutes and rewards you with a stunning panoramic view of both bays. Entrance fee is around 30 THB. Best light is in the early morning hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Long Beach (Hat Yao) on Phi Phi Don — a short longtail boat ride or a 30-minute walk. Swim, snorkel with your own rented mask and fins (rent for ~150 THB/day), and relax on the quieter stretch of sand away from the crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village for the evening. Explore the beachside bars with fire shows — many are free to watch. Grab a bucket cocktail (a Thai budget classic) from a beach bar for around 150–200 THB.

meals.breakfast: Small local café near your guesthouse — banana pancake with honey and fresh fruit shake. Budget: 80–100 THB.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from a morning market stall or grab fried rice and a cold Chang beer near Long Beach. Budget: 100–150 THB.
meals.dinner: Night market in Tonsai — try khao man gai (chicken rice), mango sticky rice for dessert. Budget: 150–180 THB.

day_by_day.notes: October is shoulder/wet season — mornings are usually clearer. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a small dry bag for beach days. Snorkeling gear rental is widely available in Tonsai Village.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group snorkeling tour around Phi Phi Leh — the smaller uninhabited island. Most half-day tours depart at 8:00–9:00 AM and cost around 400–600 THB per person. Highlights include Maya Bay (made famous by 'The Beach'), Pileh Lagoon, and Viking Cave.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the tour by early afternoon. Relax at Loh Dalum Bay — the bay on the north side of Phi Phi Don with calm turquoise water. Rent a kayak (200–300 THB/hour) and paddle around the bay at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a beachfront spot on Loh Dalum Bay. Many bars have bean bags and cheap happy hour deals between 5–7 PM. Watch the sky turn pink and orange over the water.

meals.breakfast: Eat before the tour — grab a toast with egg and coffee at a local café. Budget: 70–90 THB.
meals.lunch: Many tours include a simple lunch on a beach or boat — confirm beforehand. If not, grab a noodle soup upon return. Budget: 80–120 THB.
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant on Loh Dalum — try grilled fish with garlic and lime, served with jasmine rice. Budget: 200–250 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has limited visitor quotas and timed entry — confirm with your tour operator that it's included and accessible. Bring motion sickness tablets if you're sensitive to boat rides. Book snorkeling tours the evening before for best availability.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning — sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Then explore the quieter parts of Phi Phi Don on foot. Walk northeast toward Laem Tong Beach area or explore the fishing village side of the island away from the tourist strip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a longtail boat to Monkey Beach (Hat Hua Lan) — a short 15-minute ride from Tonsai pier (negotiate a round trip for ~200–300 THB). Watch the cheeky macaque monkeys on the rocks but keep your belongings secure. Swim in the clear water nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free Muay Thai show — many venues on Phi Phi host free or very low-cost exhibitions in the evening. Check local notice boards at your guesthouse. Afterward, grab dinner and a cold Singha beer.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or acai bowl from a health café — a slightly indulgent budget treat. Budget: 120–150 THB.
meals.lunch: Simple pad see ew (stir-fried noodles) from a street stall in Tonsai. Budget: 80–100 THB.
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant away from the main tourist strip — ask your guesthouse for recommendations. Try tom yum soup and green curry with rice. Budget: 180–220 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Avoid feeding the monkeys at Monkey Beach — it disrupts their diet and they can bite. Negotiate longtail boat prices firmly but respectfully. Check weather forecasts each morning during wet season for any boat service disruptions.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Phi Phi accommodation and take the morning ferry to Krabi Town (approx. 1.5 hours, ~250–300 THB). Arrive in Krabi Town by mid-morning. Check in to a budget guesthouse in Krabi Town (dorm beds from 200 THB, private rooms from 400–600 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Krabi Town on foot — visit the famous Krabi Town Walking Street area and the riverside promenade. Check out the quirky frog statue on the waterfront and the colorful weekend market stalls (even on weekdays some vendors are present). Visit Wat Kaew Korawaram temple — free entry, beautiful white temple with panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Krabi Town Night Market (open daily) near the waterfront for an incredible spread of cheap local food. This is one of the best street food scenes in southern Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Quick bite before ferry departure — roti with condensed milk and banana from a street cart. Budget: 40–60 THB.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local rice and curry shop (khao gaeng) in Krabi Town — point and choose from pre-cooked dishes displayed in trays. Budget: 60–80 THB.
meals.dinner: Krabi Town Night Market — try boat noodles, grilled corn, coconut ice cream, fresh fruit skewers. Budget: 120–180 THB for a full spread.

day_by_day.notes: Krabi Town is far more budget-friendly and authentic than Ao Nang. It's an excellent base for day trips. Store your luggage at the guesthouse if you arrive before check-in time. The night market is a must — go hungry.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early longtail boat to the Four Islands (Si Ko) — a popular budget day trip departing from Ao Nang or Krabi pier. The tour visits Koh Poda, Koh Gai (Chicken Island), Koh Tub, and Koh Mor. Cost: 400–600 THB including snorkeling stops and a beach lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Four Islands tour — snorkel around Koh Poda's coral reef, walk the sandbar connecting Koh Tub and Koh Mor at low tide (a magical experience), and relax on the powdery white sand of Koh Gai.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town by late afternoon. Rest and freshen up. Explore the riverside evening scene — grab a Chang beer and sit by the water watching fishing boats return.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or nearby café — toast, eggs, and coffee. Budget: 80–100 THB.
meals.lunch: Included in the Four Islands tour — typically a simple Thai buffet on the beach or a nearby restaurant. Confirm when booking.
meals.dinner: Try a local restaurant serving southern Thai cuisine — kaeng tai pla (southern fish curry) is a regional specialty. Budget: 150–200 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Four Islands tour through your guesthouse or a local travel agent — avoid overpaying at pier-side kiosks. Confirm what's included (snorkel gear, lunch, national park fee). The sandbar walk at low tide is tide-dependent — check timing with your guide.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike in Krabi Town (200–300 THB/day with helmet) and ride to Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — about 8 km from town. Climb the famous 1,237 steps to the summit for a breathtaking 360-degree view over Krabi's limestone karsts and jungle. Start early to beat the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ride to Thung Teao Forest Natural Park and swim in the emerald-green Emerald Pool (Sa Morakot) — a natural hot spring pool surrounded by jungle. Entry fee: 200 THB. Nearby is the Blue Pool (Sa Nam Phet) — a shorter, cooler hike for a stunning deep-blue thermal pool.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town on the motorbike. Browse the evening market and relax. Optional: join a cheap cooking class advertised at local guesthouses (some evening classes run 500–800 THB).

meals.breakfast: Local khao tom (rice soup) at a market stall — a classic Thai breakfast. Budget: 50–70 THB.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for the day trip — buy fresh fruit, boiled eggs, and sticky rice from a morning market. Budget: 80–100 THB.
meals.dinner: Reward yourself with a slightly nicer sit-down meal — massaman curry with roti bread at a riverside restaurant. Budget: 200–250 THB.

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple steps are steep and demanding — wear proper shoes and bring plenty of water. Start before 8 AM to avoid the midday heat. The Emerald Pool can get crowded by 10 AM — arrive early. Motorbike rental requires a passport deposit at most shops.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning minivan transfer from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approx. 2–2.5 hours including ferry crossings, ~250–350 THB). Check in to a budget bungalow or guesthouse on Koh Lanta's Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) or Klong Nin Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (50–80 THB/day) or motorbike (200 THB/day) and explore Koh Lanta's west coast beaches at your own pace. Visit Klong Nin Beach, Bamboo Bay (Ao Mai Phai), and the scenic southern tip of the island.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ban Ko Lanta — the charming Old Town on the east coast with wooden shophouses on stilts over the water. Browse art galleries, local craft shops, and enjoy the slower pace of this authentic fishing village.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure in Krabi — rice porridge or noodle soup. Budget: 50–70 THB.
meals.lunch: Beachside shack on Long Beach — fresh grilled squid with sweet chili sauce and sticky rice. Budget: 120–150 THB.
meals.dinner: Old Town restaurant in Ban Ko Lanta — try fresh seafood at local prices. Steamed fish with lime and garlic is a standout. Budget: 180–220 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta is quieter and more laid-back than Phi Phi — perfect for a change of pace. The Old Town is best visited in the late afternoon when the light is golden. Book your accommodation in advance as options are more spread out here.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of Koh Lanta — entrance fee 200 THB. Hike through mangroves and jungle trails. Visit the lighthouse for sweeping views of the Andaman Sea and surrounding islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkel at Koh Rok — a stunning twin-island national park about 45 minutes by speedboat from Koh Lanta. Day trips run around 1,000–1,200 THB including snorkeling gear and lunch. The coral reefs here are among the healthiest in the region.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your beach area and relax with a sunset cocktail. Many beachfront bars on Koh Lanta's west coast offer perfect sunset views — grab a cheap happy hour drink and watch the sun dip into the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café — fresh fruit platter and toast with peanut butter. Budget: 80–100 THB.
meals.lunch: Included in the Koh Rok day trip — typically a Thai beach picnic lunch.
meals.dinner: Night market or local restaurant near your beach — try gaeng keow wan (green curry) with jasmine rice. Budget: 150–180 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok trips are weather-dependent — check conditions the night before. The national park at the southern tip closes at 6 PM. Bring insect repellent for the mangrove walk. October can bring afternoon rain showers — plan outdoor activities for the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning on Koh Lanta. Enjoy a slow beach morning — read, swim, or simply relax. This is your built-in buffer day for rest and spontaneous exploration. Walk along Long Beach at low tide when the sand stretches wide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day kayaking tour through the mangroves and sea caves near Koh Lanta's eastern shore. Budget tours run around 400–600 THB and often include a guide who explains the mangrove ecosystem. Alternatively, rent a kayak independently for 150–200 THB/hour.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local beach bonfire or live music session — check notice boards at your guesthouse. Many beach bars on Koh Lanta host informal music nights. Enjoy a final relaxed evening on the island.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie and banana pancake at a beach café — a classic backpacker breakfast. Budget: 100–130 THB.
meals.lunch: Beachside restaurant — pad thai with shrimp and a fresh coconut. Budget: 120–150 THB.
meals.dinner: Cook your own meal if your guesthouse has a kitchen, or splurge slightly on a seafood BBQ platter at a beachfront restaurant. Budget: 250–350 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Day 10 is intentionally relaxed — budget travel can be exhausting. Use this day to do laundry (laundry services cost 40–60 THB/kg), recharge power banks, and plan your remaining days. Stock up on snacks from a 7-Eleven for cheap hydration and energy bars.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry or minivan transfer back toward Krabi, then connect onward to Ao Nang Beach — one of Krabi's most popular beach hubs. Check in to a budget guesthouse in Ao Nang (private rooms from 400–700 THB). Drop your bags and head straight to the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ao Nang Beach and the surrounding area. Walk south along the beach toward Nopparat Thara Beach — a long, less crowded stretch of sand backed by casuarina trees. Rent a sunbed (50–100 THB) or lay on your own towel for free.
day_by_day.evening: Browse Ao Nang's busy walking street — packed with street food vendors, souvenir shops, and cheap restaurants. This is a great place to pick up budget gifts and snacks. Watch street performers near the beach road.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure from Koh Lanta — noodle soup at a local stall. Budget: 50–70 THB.
meals.lunch: Beachside food stall in Ao Nang — fried rice with egg and vegetables. Budget: 80–100 THB.
meals.dinner: Ao Nang Walking Street — try boat noodles, grilled pork skewers, and mango sticky rice. Budget: 150–200 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Ao Nang is more touristy and slightly pricier than Krabi Town — compare prices before buying. Longtail boats from Ao Nang pier can reach Railay Beach (non-motorized access only, no road) in 10–15 minutes for around 100 THB per person each way.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang to Railay Beach (100 THB each way) — one of the most spectacular beaches in Thailand, accessible only by boat due to towering limestone cliffs. Explore Railay West (calm swimming beach) and Railay East (mangrove side). Hike to Railay Viewpoint — a steep 30-minute scramble rewarded with incredible views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through to Phra Nang Cave Beach — widely considered one of the most beautiful beaches in Southeast Asia. Snorkel in the crystal-clear water, explore the sacred cave shrine, and relax under the towering karst cliffs. Rent snorkel gear from beach vendors (~150 THB). Take a longtail boat back to Ao Nang in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Last big night out — celebrate your final full day with a proper Thai feast. Find a well-reviewed local restaurant in Ao Nang or Krabi Town and order a spread of your favorite dishes from the trip.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before heading to the pier — eggs, toast, and strong Thai iced coffee. Budget: 80–100 THB.
meals.lunch: Beach shack on Railay — fresh coconut, grilled corn, and a simple rice dish. Budget: 130–160 THB.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — tom kha gai (coconut milk soup), pad krapow moo (basil pork), and sticky rice with mango. Budget: 250–300 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Railay and Phra Nang are must-sees but can be crowded midday — arrive early. The viewpoint hike involves ropes and steep terrain — wear proper shoes and avoid after rain when it's slippery. Keep valuables in a waterproof bag. Longtail boats run until around 6–7 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and soak in your last views of Krabi. Pack up and check out. If time allows, do a final stroll along Ao Nang Beach or grab last-minute souvenirs from the walking street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Krabi International Airport (shared minivan ~150 THB or taxi ~300–400 THB from Ao Nang). Allow plenty of time — at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Browse airport shops for duty-free snacks and Thai tea to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, island hopping, and street food across one of the world's most stunning destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — khao tom (rice soup with ginger and egg) or a classic roti with banana and Nutella from a street cart. Budget: 60–80 THB.
meals.lunch: Airport food court — surprisingly affordable with local options available. Budget: 100–150 THB.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Double-check your flight details and departure terminal the night before. Keep some Thai baht for last-minute airport expenses — unused baht can be exchanged back at the airport. Leave a small tip for your guesthouse staff as a thank-you gesture. Total estimated daily budget: 800–1,200 THB (approx. $22–$35 USD) excluding accommodation and major tours.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and arrange transfer to Phi Phi Islands via Krabi pier. Take a high-speed ferry from Ao Nang or Rassada Pier to Phi Phi Don (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Check into your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along Tonsai Bay promenade to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Tonsai Village night scene. Browse the beachside stalls, watch fire shows on the beach, and settle into island life.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or meal at Krabi Airport before boarding the ferry
meals.lunch: Quick bite at a pier-side café near Rassada Pier — try a bowl of boat noodles or pad thai (approx. 80–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Papaya Restaurant in Tonsai Village — local Thai dishes like massaman curry and grilled fish at mid-range prices (approx. 200–350 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry transfer in advance or arrange through your hotel. Carry some Thai Baht cash for the ferry and tips. October can bring occasional rain showers — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise hike up to Phi Phi Viewpoint (Yung Kasem). The 20–30 minute climb rewards you with panoramic views of both Tonsai and Loh Dalum bays — one of Thailand's most iconic vistas. Bring water and wear sturdy sandals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day snorkeling longtail boat tour around Phi Phi Don and nearby reefs. Visit Loh Samah Bay and Pileh Lagoon, famous for their crystal-clear turquoise water and limestone cliffs. Spot colorful fish and coral.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on Loh Dalum Beach for sunset. The bay glows golden in the evening light. Head back to Tonsai for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café — fresh fruit, toast, and coffee (approx. 100–180 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack a light snack for the boat tour, or grab fresh coconut and grilled corn from beach vendors on return (approx. 60–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Try Unni's Restaurant in Tonsai Village for wood-fired pizza or fresh seafood pasta — a beloved island favorite (approx. 250–400 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the snorkeling longtail tour directly at the pier for better rates (approx. 400–600 THB per person). Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a dry bag for your phone.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full-day island hopping boat trip departing from Tonsai Pier. First stop: Maya Bay on Phi Phi Leh — the legendary beach from 'The Beach.' Arrive early before day-trip crowds swell. Swim in the bay and explore the surrounding cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Viking Cave (Tham Phaya Nak) to see ancient cave paintings and learn about the swiftlet nest harvesting tradition. Then head to Monkey Beach (Hat Ling) to observe wild macaques — keep food secured! Snorkel at Ao Ling reef on the return.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don by late afternoon. Shower and enjoy a relaxed evening at your boutique stay. Explore the village night market for handmade souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch included with most full-day boat tours, or buy fresh fruit and snacks from vendors at Maya Bay pier
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the Tonsai night market — try pad kra pao (basil stir-fry), mango sticky rice, and fresh spring rolls (approx. 150–250 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted visitor numbers and specific opening hours to protect the ecosystem. Book a licensed tour operator. Full-day tours typically cost 900–1,400 THB per person including snorkeling gear.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak from Tonsai Beach (approx. 150–200 THB/hour) and paddle around the coastline of Phi Phi Don at your own pace. Explore hidden coves, sea caves, and quiet beaches inaccessible by foot. Alternatively, join a guided kayaking tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon unwinding on Hat Yao (Long Beach) — one of Phi Phi's best beaches for swimming and sunbathing. It's a short longtail ride from Tonsai (approx. 50–80 THB each way). Read, swim, and recharge.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset from Tonsai Beach. Join the famous Phi Phi beach bar scene — enjoy a bucket cocktail at Ibiza House or Sunflower Bar while watching fire dancers perform on the sand.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie bowl and eggs at a beachside café in Tonsai (approx. 120–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Long Beach — grilled seafood or a fresh green papaya salad from a small shack restaurant (approx. 150–250 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cosmic Restaurant — known for fresh Thai seafood platters and a relaxed atmosphere. Try the grilled tiger prawns (approx. 300–450 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: October seas can be slightly choppy — check with locals about kayaking conditions before renting. Long Beach is quieter than Tonsai and ideal for a peaceful afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Phi Phi Don to Krabi Town (approx. 1.5 hours, 350–450 THB). Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Krabi Town or store luggage and explore. Visit the Krabi Town Walking Street Market if it's the weekend, or explore the riverside promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for sweeping views over Krabi's jungle and coastline. Allow 1.5–2 hours for the climb. Then explore the temple grounds and meditation caves at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Krabi Town riverside evening market. Sample local street food, watch the sun dip behind the karst mountains, and enjoy the laid-back town atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before the ferry — roti with banana and condensed milk from a Tonsai street vendor (approx. 50–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Krabi Town — try khao man gai (poached chicken rice) or tom yum soup (approx. 80–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Krabi Town Night Market (open daily) — a fantastic spread of street food stalls. Try grilled satay, pad see ew, and fresh coconut ice cream (approx. 150–250 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Tiger Cave Temple is free to enter but a donation is appreciated. Wear modest clothing to cover shoulders and knees. The climb is steep — bring water and go early to avoid midday heat. October rain can make steps slippery; rubber-soled shoes recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day Four Islands tour departing from Krabi Town or Ao Nang. Visit Koh Mor, Koh Chuak, Koh Maa, and Koh Ngai — each with distinct character from sandy beaches to coral reefs. Snorkel at multiple stops throughout the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Four Islands tour — spend the afternoon at Koh Ngai (Hai Island), the most scenic of the group, with powdery white sand and calm, clear water ideal for swimming. Some tours include a beachside barbecue lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town or Ao Nang by late afternoon. If staying in Ao Nang, explore the beach promenade, browse souvenir shops, and enjoy the sunset from the beach.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local Thai breakfast of jok (rice porridge) with a soft-boiled egg from a street cart (approx. 60–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside BBQ lunch included with most Four Islands tours, or bring snacks
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ao Nang — try Last Fisherman Bar for seafood with a beachside view, or explore the strip for mid-range Thai restaurants (approx. 250–400 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Four Islands tours typically cost 800–1,200 THB per person including snorkeling equipment and lunch. Book through a reputable agency in Krabi Town for best value. October weather is transitional — tours may occasionally be cancelled; confirm the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang Beach to Railay Beach (15-minute ride, approx. 100 THB each way) — accessible only by boat due to towering limestone cliffs. Explore Railay East and West beaches. Attempt the short hike to Railay Viewpoint for cliff-top panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Phra Nang Cave Beach — one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches, with a sacred princess cave shrine adorned with offerings. Swim in the impossibly clear water. If feeling adventurous, try rock climbing on the famous Railay limestone walls (beginner courses available from local operators, approx. 800–1,200 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Railay West Beach before taking the last longtail back to Ao Nang. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in Ao Nang.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Ao Nang before heading to the pier — fresh fruit plate and coffee at a café (approx. 120–180 THB)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside restaurant on Railay — fresh fish with steamed rice and a cold Chang beer (approx. 200–300 THB per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ao Nang — try Krua Thara Restaurant for authentic southern Thai cuisine including crab curry and stir-fried morning glory (approx. 200–350 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Railay is accessible only by longtail boat. During October, seas can be rougher — check with boatmen about conditions. Phra Nang Beach is a short walk through the jungle from Railay East. Bring cash as ATMs are limited on Railay.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a minivan or shared taxi from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approximately 2–2.5 hours including a short ferry crossing). Check into a mid-range beachside bungalow on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) or Klong Nin Beach. Drop bags and head straight to the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter (approx. 200–300 THB/day) and explore Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) — a charming stilted village of Chinese-Malay heritage with wooden shophouses, cafés, and artisan shops. Walk the old pier and browse local galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the west-facing beaches — Sunset Beach (Hat Khlong Nin) offers spectacular views. Join locals and travelers for sundowners at a beachside bar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast before departure in Ao Nang or Krabi Town — khao tom (rice soup) or a Western breakfast at a guesthouse café
meals.lunch: Lunch in Koh Lanta Old Town — try a Muslim-style southern Thai lunch of khao yam (rice salad) or fresh fish curry at a local eatery (approx. 100–180 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Time for Lime cooking school restaurant in Klong Dao — known for creative Thai dishes in a beautiful garden setting (approx. 300–450 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Minivan transfers from Krabi to Koh Lanta cost approx. 300–400 THB per person and include the short ferry crossing. Book the day before through your hotel or a travel agency. Koh Lanta is more relaxed and less touristy than Phi Phi — ideal for a slower pace.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island. Explore jungle trails, spot wildlife, and visit the historic lighthouse with views across the Andaman Sea. The park entrance fee is approx. 200 THB.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling trip to the islands off Koh Lanta — Koh Rok (if weather permits) is famous for its pristine reefs and vibrant marine life. Alternatively, visit Koh Phi Phi Leh's lesser-known equivalent: the reefs around Koh Haa (Five Islands), considered some of the best snorkeling in the region.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta and enjoy a relaxed evening. Visit the Friday Night Market in Saladan (if visiting on a Friday) or the smaller local market near the pier for street food and handicrafts.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your bungalow or a beachside café — tropical fruit plate, yogurt, and fresh juice (approx. 150–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the national park morning, or eat at the small park café. Alternatively, have lunch at a beachside shack on Long Beach (approx. 150–250 THB)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the local market — grilled corn, rotis, pad thai, and fresh coconut water (approx. 150–220 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok day trips cost approx. 1,200–1,800 THB and may be weather-dependent in October. Confirm availability with local operators. The national park is best visited in the morning before heat peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Thai cooking class on Koh Lanta — Time for Lime is a highly regarded school offering morning half-day classes (approx. 1,500–2,000 THB including market visit). Learn to make 4–5 classic Thai dishes from scratch using fresh local ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on Klong Dao Beach or Klong Nin Beach — two of Koh Lanta's most beautiful and uncrowded stretches of sand. Swim, read, or simply enjoy the Andaman Sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga session on the beach (many resorts and independent instructors offer drop-in classes, approx. 300–500 THB). Follow with a traditional Thai massage at a beachside spa (approx. 300–400 THB/hour).

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before cooking class — fresh fruit and coffee at your accommodation
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you prepared in your cooking class — a highlight of the day!
meals.dinner: Dinner at Drunken Sailors Bar & Restaurant on Klong Dao Beach — relaxed atmosphere, good Thai and Western options, live music some evenings (approx. 250–400 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least a day in advance. Time for Lime also supports a local charity — a great ethical travel choice. October evenings on Koh Lanta are warm and often beautiful after afternoon showers pass.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a ferry or speedboat from Koh Lanta to Koh Lipe (approximately 2–3 hours depending on route, approx. 700–1,000 THB). Koh Lipe is a tiny, stunning island near the Malaysian border known for its exceptional beaches and laid-back vibe. Check into a mid-range bungalow near Pattaya Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Lipe's famous Walking Street — a pedestrian lane lined with restaurants, bars, dive shops, and souvenir stalls. Rent a snorkel set (approx. 100 THB/day) and wade into the crystal-clear waters of Sunrise Beach or Pattaya Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Sunset Beach — the island's most atmospheric spot. Join the small crowd of travelers who gather here each evening. Head back to Walking Street for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast before departure from Koh Lanta — toast and eggs at your bungalow café
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry, or grab a quick bite upon arrival at a Walking Street café (approx. 100–180 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner on Walking Street — try Pooh's Bar & Restaurant for fresh grilled seafood and Thai curries at fair prices (approx. 200–350 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry schedules between Koh Lanta and Koh Lipe may be limited in October — book in advance and reconfirm. The journey may involve a transfer at Pak Bara pier. Koh Lipe is small and walkable; no motorbikes are allowed on the island.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day snorkeling or diving trip around Koh Lipe and the surrounding Tarutao National Marine Park islands. Visit Koh Adang, Koh Rawi, and Koh Hin Ngam — known for their pristine reefs, sea turtles, and colourful reef fish. Snorkeling tours approx. 800–1,200 THB; diving from approx. 2,500 THB for two dives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island hopping tour — hike to the Koh Adang viewpoint for sweeping views over the archipelago, or relax on the deserted white-sand beaches of Koh Rawi. Snorkel at a second reef site on the return journey.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening on Koh Lipe — treat yourself to a beachfront dinner. Explore Walking Street one last time, pick up souvenirs, and enjoy a cold Singha beer while watching the stars over the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your bungalow before the tour departs — fresh fruit and eggs (approx. 150–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch included with most full-day island hopping tours
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last island night — dinner at Ibiza Beach Club or a beachfront seafood restaurant on Pattaya Beach (approx. 350–550 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lipe sits within Tarutao National Marine Park — a national park fee of approx. 200 THB applies. October water visibility can be excellent between rain periods. Book your tour the evening before to secure a spot.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Lipe — wake up for one last sunrise on Sunrise Beach (the aptly named east-facing beach). Take a slow walk along the shoreline, swim in the warm shallow water, and soak in the last moments of island life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Koh Lipe by speedboat to Pak Bara pier on the mainland (approx. 1 hour, 700–900 THB), then arrange onward transport to Hat Yai Airport or Trang for your departure flight. If time allows before departure, explore Hat Yai's famous street food scene — one of southern Thailand's best.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Thailand — reflect on 13 days of island hopping, street food feasts, stunning beaches, and unforgettable sunsets across the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast on Koh Lipe — fresh papaya, sticky rice with mango, and iced Thai tea from a Walking Street stall (approx. 100–150 THB)
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in Hat Yai if time allows — famous for its grilled chicken (kai yang), roti, and dim sum (approx. 100–200 THB)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your speedboat departure time the evening before — services from Koh Lipe can vary. Allow at least 3–4 hours travel time from Koh Lipe to Hat Yai Airport. Consider booking a private transfer from Pak Bara for ease and reliability. Exchange remaining Thai Baht before departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at destination airport at 13:00 – no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat transfer from Krabi or Phuket pier to Phi Phi Islands. Check in to your boutique luxury property, unpack, and enjoy a welcome drink on the terrace overlooking the Andaman Sea. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to orient yourself with the island.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at your resort's beach bar or a clifftop bar overlooking the iconic Phi Phi Don bay. Watch the golden hour light illuminate the limestone karsts.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick premium bite at the airport lounge or a riverside restaurant near the pier before boarding your speedboat transfer.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant or a top-rated beachfront seafood restaurant on Phi Phi Don – try grilled tiger prawns, fresh catch of the day, and Thai green curry in an open-air setting.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private speedboat transfer for comfort and speed. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. October is the shoulder season – expect occasional rain showers but fewer crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat tour to Maya Bay (The Beach) – arrive early before day-trippers for a serene experience. Snorkel in the crystal-clear waters of Pileh Lagoon and explore the dramatic limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Island hop to Bamboo Island and Mosquito Island for pristine white sand beaches and excellent snorkeling over vibrant coral reefs. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by your resort on a secluded beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don and explore the lively Tonsai Village. Browse local artisan shops and enjoy the vibrant yet intimate island atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Full Thai breakfast at your boutique resort – jasmine rice congee, tropical fruit platter, fresh coconut, and eggs to order.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket arranged by your resort – artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, chilled sparkling water, and local snacks enjoyed on a private beach.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Zeavola Resort's restaurant (if accessible) or a premium beachfront restaurant – try massaman lamb, whole steamed fish with lime and chili, and mango sticky rice for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Book your private longtail boat the evening before. Maya Bay has regulated visitor hours – early arrival is essential. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, snorkel gear (or rent premium equipment), and waterproof bags.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike to the Phi Phi Don Viewpoint for panoramic views over the twin bays and the surrounding Andaman Sea. The 30-minute hike is rewarding and best done before the heat builds up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private kayaking excursion through sea caves, hidden lagoons, and mangrove tunnels around Phi Phi Leh. Your guide will navigate you through emerald-green waters inaccessible by larger boats.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a traditional Thai massage and spa treatment at your resort's wellness center. Choose from a 90-minute aromatherapy massage or a traditional Thai herbal compress treatment.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light breakfast before the hike – fresh fruit, yogurt, and Thai iced coffee from your resort.
meals.lunch: Return to the resort for a poolside lunch – tom yum soup, fresh spring rolls, and a chilled coconut water.
meals.dinner: Street food tour of Tonsai Village with a private guide – sample pad thai from a renowned local stall, grilled satay skewers, papaya salad, and fresh mango with sticky rice from market vendors.

day_by_day.notes: The viewpoint hike involves steep, uneven steps – wear proper footwear. The street food tour is a curated premium experience arranged through your concierge – they will identify the best and safest vendors for you.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat day trip to Koh Lanta – explore the Old Town's charming Sino-Portuguese shophouses, visit the Koh Lanta Marine National Park, and walk the stilted wooden boardwalk of Ban Ko Lanta.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling at the pristine reefs of Koh Rok Nai and Koh Rok Nok (part of Koh Lanta Marine National Park) – some of the most biodiverse reefs in the Andaman Sea. Look for sea turtles, reef sharks, and colorful reef fish.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise back toward Phi Phi Islands on your private speedboat with chilled champagne and canapés as the sun dips below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at your resort before departure.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a renowned restaurant in Koh Lanta Old Town – grilled barracuda, crab fried rice, and fresh lime juice.
meals.dinner: Dinner back on Phi Phi Don at a beachfront restaurant – enjoy a seafood platter with lobster, crab, and prawns grilled over charcoal, paired with Thai jasmine rice and a cold Singha beer or local wine.

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok requires a national park entry fee. The boat journey is approximately 1.5–2 hours each way. Confirm sea conditions with your captain the evening before, as October can bring choppy seas.

day_by_day.morning: Scuba diving excursion with a premium dive operator – explore the legendary dive sites around Phi Phi including Hin Phae and Bida Nok, known for leopard sharks, moray eels, and vibrant soft corals. Non-divers can opt for a guided snorkeling session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and recharge at your boutique resort – lounge by the infinity pool, read on the beach, or take a nap in a beachside hammock. Optional: book a private yoga session on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Fire show and beach party night on Tonsai Beach – a quintessential Phi Phi experience. Watch skilled performers twirl fire under a canopy of stars.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-dive breakfast at the resort – toast, fruit, and fresh juice.
meals.lunch: Post-dive lunch at a dive center café or resort – pad kra pao (basil stir-fry) with a fried egg and steamed rice.
meals.dinner: Beachside BBQ dinner – choose from premium cuts of meat and fresh seafood laid out on ice, grilled to order. Pair with Thai papaya salad and sticky rice.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm dive certification requirements in advance. PADI-certified dive operators on Phi Phi offer both fun dives and introductory dives for beginners. Bring an underwater camera or rent one from the dive shop.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phi Phi Islands by private speedboat to Krabi Town. Check in to a luxury property in Krabi (e.g., Rayavadee or a premium Railay Beach resort). Explore the dramatic Railay Beach, accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rock climbing session on the famous limestone karsts of Railay Beach with a certified guide – suitable for beginners and experienced climbers alike. Enjoy breathtaking views of the Andaman Sea from the cliff tops.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Railay West Beach at sunset – one of the most stunning sunsets in Thailand. Enjoy cocktails at a beachfront bar as the sky turns shades of orange and pink.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast on Phi Phi before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant in Railay Beach – try fresh seafood tom kha soup, prawn pad thai, and fresh coconut ice cream.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rayavadee's Grotto Restaurant (set inside a natural cave) or a top-rated Railay Beach restaurant – multi-course Thai tasting menu with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is only accessible by longtail boat from Krabi Town or Ao Nang – a short and scenic 15-minute ride. Book your luxury accommodation in Railay or Krabi well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Four Islands Tour by private longtail boat from Railay – visit Koh Poda, Chicken Island (Koh Kai), Tup Island, and Phra Nang Cave Beach. Swim, snorkel, and explore each island's unique character.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the sacred Phra Nang Cave on Railay Beach – a stunning sea cave adorned with colorful offerings. Swim in the clear turquoise waters of Phra Nang Beach, consistently ranked among the world's most beautiful beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Longtail boat back to Ao Nang for a street food evening. Explore Ao Nang's vibrant night market and sample local delicacies with a private food guide.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Railay resort – eggs benedict with smoked salmon, tropical fruit, and fresh-brewed Thai coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on Koh Poda Island – prepared by your resort or purchased from a local vendor: fresh sandwiches, fruit, and chilled beverages.
meals.dinner: Street food tour in Ao Nang – grilled squid, pad see ew noodles, coconut ice cream in a cone, mango sticky rice, and fresh-squeezed sugarcane juice from market stalls.

day_by_day.notes: Tup Island is accessible by foot at low tide – check tide times in advance. The street food tour should be arranged through your concierge for a curated and safe culinary experience.

day_by_day.morning: Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) excursion – climb 1,237 steps to the summit for a breathtaking 360-degree panoramic view of Krabi Province's jungle, rice paddies, and the Andaman Sea. Visit the meditation caves at the base.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking through the mangroves of Ao Thalane Bay – paddle through serene waterways, spot wildlife including kingfishers and mudskippers, and explore hidden lagoons accessible only by kayak.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your luxury resort for a private in-room or beachside spa treatment – traditional Thai massage with herbal compress and aromatherapy oils.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the temple climb – light options such as fresh fruit, yogurt, and green tea.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant near Ao Thalane – fresh fish curry, steamed rice, and iced Thai milk tea.
meals.dinner: Romantic dinner for two at your resort's signature restaurant – enjoy a chef's tasting menu featuring modern Thai cuisine with locally sourced ingredients and a curated wine list.

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous – start early to avoid midday heat. Dress modestly for the temple (shoulders and knees covered). The mangrove kayaking tour takes approximately 3–4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Krabi to Koh Lipe via speedboat or ferry (approximately 3–4 hours). Koh Lipe is a remote, pristine island in the Tarutao Marine National Park – often called the 'Maldives of Thailand.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your luxury beachfront resort on Koh Lipe (e.g., Idyllic Concept Resort or Bundhaya Speed Boat Resort). Take a first dip in the impossibly clear waters of Sunrise Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Walking Street – Koh Lipe's charming pedestrian strip lined with restaurants, bars, and boutique shops. Sample local street food and enjoy the laid-back island vibe.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Krabi hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on board the ferry or at a café near the departure pier.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a top-rated restaurant on Walking Street – try fresh grilled lobster, southern Thai curry (gaeng tai pla), and a refreshing fruit smoothie.

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lipe is remote and less developed – this is part of its charm. ATMs are limited, so carry sufficient cash. The journey from Krabi may involve a combination of land and sea transfers – confirm the route with your travel agent.

day_by_day.morning: Private snorkeling and island hopping tour around the Tarutao Marine National Park – visit Koh Adang, Koh Rawi, and Koh Hin Ngam (the pebble beach island). The coral reefs here are among the most pristine in Thailand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Pattaya Beach or Sunrise Beach – both offer powdery white sand and crystal-clear turquoise water. Optional: stand-up paddleboarding or freediving lesson with a local instructor.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar on Sunset Beach. Watch the sun melt into the Andaman Sea in one of the most spectacular settings in Southeast Asia.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your resort – tropical fruit, fresh-baked pastries, and a smoothie bowl.
meals.lunch: Seafood BBQ lunch on a secluded beach during your island hopping tour – freshly caught fish and prawns grilled over an open fire.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at your resort or a top Walking Street restaurant – multi-course meal featuring southern Thai specialties, fresh seafood, and local desserts.

day_by_day.notes: Koh Hin Ngam's pebbles are believed to be sacred – do not remove them from the island. Tarutao National Park requires an entry fee. Snorkeling gear is available for rent but bringing your own mask and snorkel ensures the best fit.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the beach followed by a Thai cooking class – learn to prepare 4–5 classic Thai dishes including tom yum soup, green curry, and mango sticky rice with a local chef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Lipe's coral reefs on a certified scuba diving excursion – the dive sites around Koh Adang and Stonehenge Reef offer exceptional visibility and diverse marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell beach bonfire dinner arranged by your resort – a private setup with a personalized menu, lanterns, and live acoustic music under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga breakfast – fresh fruit, nuts, and herbal tea.
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared in the cooking class for lunch – a truly authentic farm-to-table (or sea-to-table) experience.
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire dinner – grilled whole fish, lobster, Thai salads, and a selection of Thai desserts. Champagne and cocktails included.

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class and private beach dinner through your resort concierge in advance. The beach bonfire dinner is a premium experience that requires prior arrangement and a designated safe area on the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Lipe – take a slow walk along Sunrise Beach at dawn, swim in the calm morning sea, and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Speedboat transfer back to the mainland (Hat Yai or Pak Bara pier), then private transfer to Phuket or Bangkok for your final night. Check in to a luxury 5-star hotel (e.g., The Sarojin, Amanpuri in Phuket, or Capella Bangkok).
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop bar experience in Phuket or Bangkok – enjoy panoramic city or sea views with signature cocktails. In Bangkok, visit a celebrated rooftop bar such as Vertigo at Banyan Tree or Octave at Marriott.

meals.breakfast: Grand final island breakfast at your Koh Lipe resort – full Thai and Western buffet with fresh juices and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant near your transfer point or en route – local southern Thai cuisine featuring rich coconut curries and fresh seafood.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Michelin-starred or critically acclaimed restaurant – in Bangkok, consider Gaggan Anand, Nahm, or Le Normandie for an extraordinary culinary finale to your Thailand journey.

day_by_day.notes: The transfer from Koh Lipe to Phuket or Bangkok involves multiple legs – confirm all connections and timings with your travel agent. Allow buffer time for potential delays due to ferry schedules.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning – sleep in, enjoy a luxurious hotel breakfast, and take a final dip in the pool. Last-minute souvenir shopping at a premium mall or artisan market (e.g., ICONSIAM or Chatuchak Weekend Market in Bangkok, or Jungceylon in Phuket).
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure preparation – private airport transfer in a luxury vehicle. Arrive at the airport with ample time for check-in and duty-free shopping. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of beaches, islands, and incredible Thai cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry-on snacks: pick up premium Thai snacks and treats from the airport – dried mango, coconut wafers, and artisan Thai tea for the journey home.

meals.breakfast: Sumptuous hotel breakfast – eggs cooked to order, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and premium Thai coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or airport lounge – tom kha soup, fresh spring rolls, and iced coconut water.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner before departure – choose from Thai or international options available at the premium terminal.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight details and check-in times. Use the airport's premium fast-track immigration service if available. Ensure all purchased items comply with airline carry-on and luggage regulations. Keep a small amount of Thai Baht for any last-minute expenses.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
